boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase outdoor and public-program options near the University of Portland, using City of Portland access information and University-hosted free-event listings.

cards.title: Walk the Cathedral Park Nature Patch
cards.subtitle: Cathedral Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: Meet beneath the St. Johns Bridge and take the gravel-and-path loop through the garden spaces; keep the plan to walking and looking, with no reservation needed.
cards.short_summary: A planted walk beneath the bridge with paths, picnic nooks, and river-adjacent views.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks identifies the Nature Patch as garden spaces with a gravel pathway and says Cathedral Park is open 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Use the park during its posted 5 a.m.–midnight hours. The boat-ramp lot has a fee; arrive on foot, bike, transit, or use another legal option.

cards.title: Bring a no-purchase picnic-table hang
cards.subtitle: Cathedral Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: Pick an unreserved table, bring water or something from home, and leave the spot ready for the next group; a reservation is only for guaranteed use.
cards.short_summary: A first-come outdoor table hang under the bridge.
cards.evidence_claim: The park lists picnic tables, and Portland Parks says individual picnic tables are available first-come, first-served; reservations are for guaranteed use.
cards.access_notes: Choose an individual, unreserved table. A permit is required for a guaranteed site, equipment setup, alcohol, advertising, or large gatherings.

cards.title: Follow the paths at Columbia Park Nature Patch
cards.subtitle: Columbia Park and Annex, North Portland
cards.notes: Walk the nature patch’s path network and pause at the log benches or boulders; this works well as a low-key conversation stop without bringing equipment.
cards.short_summary: A compact garden walk among trees, planted areas, and informal seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes Columbia Park Nature Patch as having log benches, boulders, walking paths, and pollinator-focused plantings; park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.source_title: Columbia Park and Annex | Portland Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted park hours. Stay on established paths and observe posted closures or field reservations.

cards.title: Use an unreserved Columbia Park table
cards.subtitle: Columbia Park and Annex, North Portland
cards.notes: Claim one available individual table for a chat or study break; if a group needs a guaranteed site, check the City’s reservation rules instead of assuming it is open.
cards.short_summary: A flexible, first-come table meet-up in a 35-acre city park.
cards.evidence_claim: Columbia Park lists picnic tables, while Portland Parks states individual picnic tables in many parks are available first-come, first-served.
cards.access_notes: No reservation is needed for an available individual table; permits apply when a group needs guaranteed use or meets listed permit conditions.

cards.title: Shoot around at McKenna Park
cards.subtitle: McKenna Park, University Park neighborhood
cards.notes: Bring a ball from home and use the outdoor court for a casual shoot-around; yield to others and avoid treating any field or court as reserved unless posted.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor basketball-court stop near UP’s University Park neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks lists a basketball court at McKenna Park and says the resurfaced court is complete and ready for play; park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Bring your own ball. The City directs visitors to reserve a sports field only when they need a reservation.

cards.title: Take a loop on McKenna’s paved paths
cards.subtitle: McKenna Park, University Park neighborhood
cards.notes: Use the paved paths for an easy walking-and-talking loop, then leave space around active games and playground users; plan around the City’s posted park hours.
cards.short_summary: A simple no-equipment walking loop close to campus.
cards.evidence_claim: McKenna Park’s City listing includes paved paths and gives park hours of 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: No equipment or reservation is needed for walking; observe any temporary closures and leash rules.

cards.title: Walk the open lawn and paths at University Park
cards.subtitle: University Park, Portsmouth
cards.notes: Meet at the park entrance on N Foss Avenue and make a relaxed lap on the paved paths; the open lawn gives a straightforward place to sit and talk.
cards.short_summary: A nearby 11-acre municipal park with paths and open lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes University Park as having mature trees, open lawn areas, a playground, and park paths; its posted hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.source_title: North Portland Parks Improvement Projects | Portland Parks & Recreation
cards.access_notes: Use the park during posted hours and avoid organized-field activity. No purchase or admission is listed for walking the public park.

cards.title: Walk Portsmouth Park together
cards.subtitle: Portsmouth Park, North Portland
cards.notes: Use the public park for a short walking-and-chat break, keeping clear of scheduled field use and leaving pets leashed; no special gear is needed for the walk.
cards.short_summary: A compact neighborhood-park walk with open sports fields.
cards.evidence_claim: Portsmouth Park is a City park with soccer and softball fields and posted hours of 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Walking does not require a reservation; the City advises reserving a sports field when a group needs one.

cards.title: Take a shaded walk at Pier Park
cards.subtitle: Pier Park, St. Johns
cards.notes: Choose the park’s shaded trails for a longer walk with a friend; keep to paths, share space with other visitors, and skip the pool or rentals for a no-purchase visit.
cards.short_summary: A forested 85-acre park walk in North Portland.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes Pier Park’s shaded trails and lists paved and unpaved paths; park hours are 5 a.m.–midnight.
cards.access_notes: Use trails during park hours. This card excludes the pool and reservable picnic site; a walk requires no purchase or admission.

cards.entity_name: University Park Neighborhood Association general meeting
cards.title: Attend a University Park neighborhood meeting
cards.subtitle: Chiles Center, University of Portland
cards.notes: Check the association’s listing before going, then attend to hear neighborhood discussion and meet local residents; the City states that everyone is welcome.
cards.short_summary: A public neighborhood conversation hosted at UP’s Chiles Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Portland says University Park Neighborhood Association general meetings are held at UP’s Chiles Center, are open to the public, and welcome everyone.
cards.source_title: University Park neighborhood | City of Portland
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current date, location, and format with the association before attending; the City’s listing says general meetings are open to the public.

warnings: For park cards, cost-free status covers the listed walking, table, and casual-use activity only; reservable sites, sports fields, parking, pools, and equipment can have separate rules or costs.
